title: Consolidate only excess terminal Uniform runs
question: Does a bounded pending catalog and shorter intermediate materialization improve complete out-of-memory native terminal Uniform?
summary: In 8 GiB m96 paired measurements, elapsed fell 17.24%, CPU 1.26% and both directions of managed temp traffic 37.01%. Reported RSS rose 4,564 KiB, working charge 92,378 bytes, and refaults 60.84%. Kept as an opt-in Linux experiment locally.

workloads: 8 GiB terminal Uniform then Balanced(8), one worker, 96 MiB engine and 1 GiB hard no-swap cgroup. 512 initial runs and native raw spill.

validation.summary: Matched full all-field/order contract, exact quotas, serialized caps, manifest and cleanup. Focused native bound, temp-space and low descriptor controls, native storage tests and compact-spill compilation.

limitations: WSL2/ext4, fixed-width single-worker fixture and uncontrolled backing caches.
The experiment combines a higher active-reader ceiling with shorter intermediate materialization. This comparison cannot attribute individual improvements to either change.
This decision covers the 8 GiB measured pairs. The separate 40 GiB transfer check has its own scope.
exclusions: Small and full warmup pairs, oracle and fixture identity outside complete-job timing.
reopen_when: Requalify under different initial run counts, platform resource bounds and memory settings before any default delivery decision.
